title: Four years off drums, and the Golden Leaf band after Eddie Jackson
summary: Stopping drums for four or five years without losing his ability; his Golden Leaf bass drum; after Jackson died he managed the Golden Leaf band.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Early drum kits and the gear drummers used

blocks.x: Now, I stayed off a drum, oh, about four or five years. I just thought, since everybody worried me, you know, playing snare, you know, street playing. And I'm just as good as I was before. Sure. It just ended. Yeah, that's right. Yeah, everybody's surprised, you know. But I figured what's in you, you know, it's just in you, that's all.
Did you keep your drums all that time?
Well, I got my snare here, but I got a boy, he used the rest of my drums. I keep my snare. See, and I got a little bass drum.
On one bass drum we saw that you played once, I mean you'd have gold and... That's my drum, that was my drum. The Golden Ruler on that. Yeah, that's mine. Golden Leaf. Golden Leaf.

Yeah, that's my drum. Golden Leaf. Yeah, but we had, after Tuxedo, we went out and Tuxedo existed, though, we made the band of Golden Leaf. You know, I was managing the band after Eddie died. So after he died, we changed, after John went to the Young Tuxedo, I changed my band to Golden Leaf. And I managed to tell him, some of the fellas passed away, so. I just quit fooling. And I let, uh, how... Oh, how...
I thought he kept my drum, finally did away with it now. I don't know where it's at.
